subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should session archive/rotation automation be supported as a core Cron event schedule, as a plugin `session_end` workflow with a narrow missing SDK seam, or not as a new OpenClaw core surface?
rationale: Current main has the lifecycle hook primitive but not the requested cron subscription surface, and the permanent shape affects public cron config, plugin API boundaries, archived transcript metadata, and security review.

options.title: Use plugin lifecycle plus narrow SDK seam
options.body: Bless plugin `session_end` as the session-boundary signal and add only the smallest SDK scheduling or event-dispatch capability that external plugins need to run this workflow safely.

options.title: Add core cron lifecycle schedules
options.body: Define `schedule.kind: event` for session archive/rotation in the Gateway protocol, with scoped metadata, permissions, persistence, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Close as plugin-owned workflow
options.body: If maintainers decide current plugin hooks already cover the use case, route the self-improving memory workflow to a ClawHub plugin and close this core request after documenting the supported pattern.

recommendation.title: Use plugin lifecycle plus narrow SDK seam
recommendation.body: Bless plugin `session_end` as the session-boundary signal and add only the smallest SDK scheduling or event-dispatch capability that external plugins need to run this workflow safely.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits at the plugin/API/core boundary where this person has the strongest recent hook and SDK history plus a related maintainer decision.
